title: Optimal competitive ratio of online bin packing
formal: Determine the infimum asymptotic competitive ratio R_BP of deterministic online bin packing.
definitions: An input is any finite sequence σ of real sizes in (0,1], revealed one at a time with no advance length information. A deterministic online policy assigns each arriving item irrevocably to a unit-capacity bin, using only the revealed prefix and its prior assignments. It cannot split or move items. Policies are arbitrary mathematical functions of histories; no computational bound is imposed. Cost A(σ) is the number of nonempty bins and OPT(σ) is the minimum for an offline packing. Define R_BP=inf{r≥1: there are a policy A and a finite constant b≥0 with A(σ)≤r OPT(σ)+b for every σ}. The same b works for all sequence lengths and sizes. The empty sequence has zero cost. This is an asymptotic ratio; it allows a uniform additive constant.
answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute distance from the defined optimal ratio is at most 1/100. Certified upper and lower bounds with gap at most 1/50 qualify via their midpoint. Bounds must cover all instances and all competing policies as quantified; attaining the infimum or supremum is not required.
context: The lower-bound paper studies the classical online model and improves the general deterministic asymptotic lower bound.
why: The constant measures the irreducible loss caused by committing to packing decisions without future items.

import_provenance.original_title: The optimal competitive ratio of online bin packing
import_provenance.original_statement: Determine the smallest asymptotic competitive ratio for deterministic online bin packing, with each arriving item irrevocably placed in a unit-capacity bin. The gap between the approximately 1.54278 lower bound and 1.57829 upper bound remains the central target of this research line.

sentences: Items of sizes at most one arrive without future information.
Each item must be placed permanently into a unit bin.

A single additive constant is allowed for all inputs.
